records.text: The Khazars were a nomadic Turkic tribe that adopted Judaism in the eighth century.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Khazars were a nomadic Turkic tribe who adopted Judaism in the 8th century.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Reference works describe the Khazars as a Turkic-speaking steppe polity whose ruling elite adopted Judaism, probably in the mid-to-late eighth century. Calling the entire people a nomadic tribe and implying population-wide conversion overstates a more complex polity and an elite-led, incompletely documented conversion.

sources.title: YIVO Encyclopedia: Khazaria
sources.relevance: Supports Turkic language and an eighth-century conversion among important segments of the Khazar elite while qualifying the statement's broader wording.

records.text: The six-pointed Star of David was not associated with Judaism until the seventeenth century.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: which show you that the Star of David, it has never been, it was never associated with Judaism. ... It even says this on Wikipedia that this did not emerge until the 17th century,

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The hexagram did not become a broadly recognized Jewish emblem until the early modern period, but its association with Jewish communities predates the seventeenth century. The Prague Jewish community was granted a flag bearing the symbol in 1354, and medieval synagogue and manuscript uses are documented. The categorical 'not associated until' claim is therefore false.

sources.title: Encyclopedia Judaica entry: Magen David
sources.relevance: Documents Jewish communal and synagogue uses in the fourteenth century, directly contradicting the claim of no association before the seventeenth century.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed (host, direct claim). APA's history timeline identifies Wilhelm Wundt's 1879 Leipzig laboratory as the beginning of formal scientific psychology and documents numerous founders and milestones. sources.title: American Psychological Association History Timeline
sources.relevance: Authoritative field history identifying Wundt's laboratory and the multi-person development of scientific psychology.
